When Stoatmod removes an image, the case now shows it behind a content warning, so moderators can see what was removed. Graphic violence is kept as a reduced copy; explicit nudity only as a small thumbnail that is permanently blurred, and the original is never stored. Both are deleted after 30 days.
Uploaded files and images, such as report evidence and case evidence, are now deleted after 30 days unless an open appeal needs them.
When a global ban can't be applied because Stoatmod's role is not above the member's, the server owner is told how to fix it.
The status page no longer marks a whole day red for a short blip: days turn amber after 5 minutes of downtime and red after an hour, and planned maintenance is shown separately.

When message moderation is enabled, Stoatmod reads message text, links, website domains and account mentions. It uses message and channel IDs and timestamps to identify the content and carry out an action. Image checks are on by default and process image attachments, animated GIF frames and link-preview pictures; server owners can turn them off for the whole server or for individual channels. When an image is removed for graphic violence, a reduced copy is kept with the case so the server's moderators and Stoatmod's operators can review it behind a content warning. When an image is removed for explicit nudity, only a small, permanently blurred thumbnail is kept and the original is never stored. Images that may involve minors are never stored. AI checks produce safety categories and model scores.
